title: HR Specialist - CS Recruitment & People Operations (Clark, Office-based)
description:
Full job description

About HK 24-BPO



HK 24-BPO is a fast-growing customer service outsourcing company serving cross-border e-commerce brands. We partner with Amazon and Shopify sellers across smart electronics, smart home, wearables, and audio product categories. Backed by our proprietary AI + human customer service system, we deliver reliable, high-quality support to customers around the world. We are now expanding our team and looking for a dedicated HR Specialist to join us in Clark.



About the Job



We are hiring an office-based HR Specialist in Clark, Pampanga. This is not a remote position — you will work from our office and play a key role in managing the full recruitment cycle and daily HR operations for our growing customer service team.



What You'll Do:



- Source, screen, and recruit customer service representatives across multiple channels (OnlineJobs.ph, referrals, social media, etc.)

- Manage the end-to-end hiring process — from posting job ads to scheduling interviews and onboarding new hires

- Maintain employee records, attendance tracking, and performance documentation

- Handle day-to-day HR administrative tasks and employee relations

- Coordinate with the management team in China to align hiring priorities and timelines

- Support training coordination and new hire orientation

- Build and maintain a talent pipeline for ongoing hiring needs

What You Bring:



- 1–2 years of experience in HR, recruitment, or talent acquisition

- Experience hiring for customer service or BPO roles is a strong plus

- Excellent communication skills in English, both written and verbal

- Highly organized with strong attention to detail

- Comfortable working with spreadsheets, job boards, and communication tools

- Self-driven and able to work independently in a fast-paced environment

- Based in or willing to relocate to Clark, Pampanga

What We Offer:



- Competitive salary: $500 – $600 per month

- Office-based position in Clark — stable, professional work environment

- Clear career growth path — grow into a senior HR role as the team scales

- Be part of a tech-driven company that combines AI with human expertise

- Hands-on experience building a team from the ground up

Availability: Full-time, office-based in Clark. Working hours to be discussed.

title: Senior Accountant
description:
Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Senior Accountant to join our accounting practice.

This is a senior, hands-on role suited to an accountant who can take ownership of client work from start to finish, review work prepared by bookkeepers and junior accountants, and provide guidance and training to team members.

The successful candidate will be technically capable, organised and confident working independently. You will be expected to manage your own workload, identify and resolve issues, meet deadlines, and deliver high-quality work without requiring ongoing supervision or step-by-step direction.



You will work closely with the Director and Client Managers while also acting as a senior point of support for our bookkeeping and accounting team.



Key Responsibilities:

Accounting & Tax Compliance

• Manage accounting and tax compliance work for a portfolio of clients from commencement through to completion.

• Prepare and review annual financial statements, including profit and loss statements, balance sheets and supporting workpapers.

• Prepare and review company, trust, partnership and individual income tax returns.

• Prepare and review BAS and IAS lodgements and other ATO compliance obligations.

• Review general ledgers, reconciliations and bookkeeping records and identify errors, inconsistencies and areas requiring further investigation.

• Perform tax reconciliations and ensure accounting records are appropriately prepared for year-end compliance.

• Identify relevant tax issues and make appropriate adjustments or recommendations.

• Ensure work is completed accurately and in accordance with Australian taxation requirements, accounting principles and internal practice standards.

• Manage assigned jobs and lodgement deadlines proactively.

Review & Quality Control

• Review work prepared by bookkeepers and junior accountants before submission for final review or lodgement.

• Identify errors and provide clear review notes explaining what needs to be corrected and why.

• Ensure workpapers and supporting documentation are complete, accurate and appropriately documented.

• Identify recurring issues in team members' work and provide practical guidance to improve future performance.

• Maintain a high standard of accuracy and consistency across client files.

Team Guidance & Development

• Provide day-to-day technical guidance to bookkeepers and junior accountants.

• Train and mentor team members in bookkeeping, reconciliations, BAS preparation, year-end accounts and tax compliance processes.

• Assist team members in developing stronger problem-solving and technical accounting skills.

• Delegate appropriate tasks and follow up to ensure work is completed correctly and on time.

• Help establish efficient and consistent processes across the accounting team.



About You

To succeed in this role, you will be someone who can be given responsibility for a job and take ownership of getting it 

completed correctly and on time.

You will be comfortable reviewing the work of others, identifying issues and providing constructive guidance to less experienced team members.

You will ideally have:

• Strong experience in Australian public practice accounting.

• Strong knowledge of Australian taxation, GST, BAS and general accounting requirements.

• Experience preparing financial statements and income tax returns for companies, trusts, partnerships and individuals.

• Demonstrated experience reviewing accounting, bookkeeping and tax compliance work prepared by other team members.

• Experience supervising, training or mentoring bookkeepers and/or junior accountants.

• Strong reconciliation and problem-solving skills.

• Excellent attention to detail and the ability to identify issues rather than simply process information.

• Strong organisational and time-management skills.

title: Senior Shopify Store Builder & Theme Designer
description:
Full-Time | Remote | Fashion E-commerce



About us



BJ-ECOM is a growing e-commerce company with a team of 30+ people working across marketing, operations, product, customer support, and development.



We operate multiple Shopify stores in Europe, the United States, and other international markets. Most of our stores are in fashion, and we are currently expanding the way we build and improve our Shopify themes across a large portfolio of brands.



We are looking for a full-time Shopify Store Builder & Theme Designer who can do more than basic Shopify editing.



We need someone who can build complete stores, customize themes properly, make strong design decisions, and create storefronts that feel clean, modern, trustworthy, and easy to shop from.



This role is a mix of store building, theme design, UX thinking, and structured execution.



What You’ll Work On



You will help us build and improve Shopify stores for different fashion brands and markets.



Your work will include setting up new stores, customizing Shopify themes, improving layouts, adapting designs for different brand identities, and making sure each store looks professional on both desktop and mobile.



You will also help us create reusable structures so we can build faster without making every store look the same.



The goal is not to copy and paste one design across every brand. We want a strong system, but each store still needs its own identity.



Responsibilities



Build 3–5 Shopify stores or theme builds per week



Customize Shopify Theme Store themes and high-quality third-party themes



Create clean, modern, mobile-first storefronts



Build homepages, collection pages, product pages, navigation, and basic store structure



Improve spacing, typography, layout flow, and overall visual hierarchy



Adapt themes for different fashion brands, countries, and languages



Keep the Shopify backend clean and organized



Follow internal systems and SOPs



Make sure stores are structured in a way that is suitable for

Google Merchant Center



Work independently and communicate clearly about progress or blockers



What We’re Looking For



3+ years of experience building or designing Shopify stores



Strong experience with Shopify theme customization



Experience with fashion e-commerce stores



A portfolio with Shopify stores you personally worked on



Good eye for layout, spacing, typography, and brand feel



Understanding of mobile-first design and e-commerce UX



Ability to work quickly without making messy stores



Comfortable working with clear systems and repeatable structures



Reliable, detail-oriented, and able to take ownership

Long-term availability



Experience working with multiple countries or languages is a plus.



This Role Is Not a Fit If



You only know how to drag and drop sections

You cannot show stores you personally built or designed

You have no fashion e-commerce experience

You depend on constant step-by-step instructions

You build stores without thinking about UX or conversion

You are only looking for short-term freelance projects



What We Offer



Full-time remote position



Long-term work with a growing e-commerce company



Stable flow of Shopify projects



Clear internal systems and workflows



Direct communication with experienced e-commerce operators



Opportunity to work on many international fashion stores



A role with real ownership and responsibility



Several people on our team have been with us for 4–5 years, so we are looking for someone who also wants to build something long-term with us.



Store Style We Like



The style we usually aim for is clean, fashion-focused, easy to navigate, and conversion-oriented.

title: Social Media Manager
description:
Social Media Operator / Manager — Part-Time Weekend Coverage



Company: Harmony



Location: Remote



Type: Full time contractor



Schedule: Saturday–Wednesday availability required



Pay: Based on experience, availability, and scope



Harmony is a fast-growing spiritual media and transformation brand built around sound, frequency, presence, and joy.

Led by musician and creator Banah Winn, Harmony reaches millions of people each month through short-form content that helps regulate the nervous system, calm the mind, and bring people back into their bodies.



We’re looking for a reliable Social Media Operator / Manager to help keep Harmony’s posting rhythm consistent across TikTok, Instagram,
, and YouTube Shorts — with strong weekend coverage required.



This is a hands-on execution role first. Most content will already be created, but we also want someone who understands short-form content, hooks, platform differences, and what makes content perform.



What You’ll Be Doing:



You’ll help manage Harmony’s daily social media flow across:

TikTok

Instagram Reels





YouTube Shorts



This may include:

Uploading videos natively inside each platform

Posting content consistently using our system

Pasting captions and adjusting formatting when needed

Adding simple covers or in-app text

Posting stories

Reposting testimonials and community reactions

Checking comments

Light community engagement

Handling or assisting with TikTok DM outreach

Flagging support-related issues to the right team member

Helping identify hooks, formats, or content patterns that are working

Most creative assets will be provided, but we are looking for someone who can think clearly about short-form content and eventually help improve the system over time.



Who This Role Is For

You’ll be a good fit if you:

Are reliable and available Saturday–Wednesday

Can consistently cover weekends

Enjoy structure, repetition, and clear systems

Are comfortable posting natively inside TikTok, Instagram,
, and YouTube

Understand short-form content and what makes people stop scrolling

Have strong attention to detail

Communicate clearly

Can follow a system without needing constant supervision

Care about spiritual, healing, sound, meditation, or personal transformation-based content

Want to grow with one brand over time

This role is not just about casually reposting content. We’re looking for someone who can help carry the rhythm of a real media brand with care and consistency.

Requirements

Availability Saturday through Wednesday

Strong comfort with TikTok, Instagram Reels,
, and YouTube Shorts

Experience posting or managing short-form content

Fast, stable internet for uploading video files

Strong organization and attention to detail

Comfortable with repetitive daily workflows

Interest in sound, frequency, music, meditation, spirituality, or personal development

Ability to communicate clearly and take ownership

Compensation & Structure

Part-time contractor role

Paid weekly or on an agreed schedule

Compensation based on experience, availability, and final scope

Initial trial period before long-term continuation

100% remote





Please answer the questions thoughtfully. The strongest applicants will show that they understand short-form content, can follow a clear system, and genuinely connect with Harmony’s mission.

title: Content Marketer
description:
About the Role



Deskwork is looking for a Marketing Specialist who creates content for a living and who is comfortable being the face of it.



This is a content-first, video-first role. The majority of the work is producing video: scripting it, filming it, editing it, and appearing in it. You will be on camera regularly: talking-head explainers, short-form social video, founder-style pieces, product and service walkthroughs, and event or behind-the-scenes content. If being on camera is not something you enjoy, this is not the role for you.



Around that core, you will run Deskwork's social channels, design supporting graphics, and manage
 campaigns for the Australia and New Zealand market. The goal is brand awareness, engagement, and inbound leads.





Key Responsibilities

-Video Content & On-Camera Presence (primary focus)

-Appear on camera as a regular presenter for Deskwork content: explainers, short-form social video, and campaign pieces.

-Script, film, and edit short-form video (Reels, Shorts, LinkedIn video, TikTok-style formats) on a consistent weekly cadence.

-Produce long-form video where required webinars, interviews, case studies, walkthroughs and cut it down into multiple short-form assets.

-Direct and coach others on camera, including the founder, leadership, and offshore team members, so recording sessions run efficiently.

-Own the full video pipeline end to end: concept, script, shoot, edit, captions, thumbnails, publishing.

-Maintain a consistent on-screen presentation style: clear delivery, good framing, clean audio, brand-consistent look.



Content Creation & Repurposing

-Turn one idea into many assets: one recording becomes clips, carousels, posts, and
 content.

-Write scripts and hooks that hold attention in the first three seconds.

-Extract content ideas from inside the business: client wins, staff stories, operational insights, founder POV and turn them into publishable content.

-Maintain a running content calendar and a backlog of ideas ready to shoot.



Social Media Management

-Own day-to-day posting across LinkedIn, Instagram,
, TikTok, and YouTube.

-Grow and engage the community: respond to comments and messages, and build relationships with the AU & NZ audience.

-Track performance and report on what is working, with clear recommendations for the next cycle.



Social Strategy & Trend Research

-Monitor trends, formats, and competitor activity across Australia and New Zealand.

-Identify trending topics and content styles worth adapting, and move quickly on them.

-Test new formats and optimise based on performance data.



Graphic Design

-Create graphics for social,
, and digital campaigns using Canva (brand templates provided).

-Design thumbnails, captions, and on-screen text that support the video content.

-Keep all visual output consistent with brand guidelines.



 Marketing

-Build, schedule, and manage
 campaigns.

-Segment audiences and build targeted
 flows.

-Monitor open rates, CTR, and conversions, and optimise accordingly.

-Maintain and grow
 lists in line with data regulations.



Qualifications & Skills



Essential

-3+ years in content marketing, social media, or video content production.

-Strong video editing skills (CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut, DaVinci Resolve, or similar).

-Strong scripting and copywriting, especially short-form hooks and conversational delivery.

title: Facebook Ads Creative Strategist (Static + Video)
description:
# Genghis Digital

## OnlineJobs.ph Job Ad:
 Ads Creative Strategist



---



## JOB TITLE (pick one)



**Primary:**

>
 Ads Creative Strategist (Static + Video, Copywriting Led)



**Alternatives:**

> Meta Ads Creative Strategist | Copy, Statics, Reels | AU Agency, Long Term

>

> Direct Response Creative Strategist for Meta Ads (Canva, Video, Copy)



*Note: OnlineJobs.ph search runs on keywords. Keep 
 Ads" or "Meta Ads" plus "Creative Strategist" in the title. Put "graphic designer" or "video editor" in there and you'll get 200 of the wrong applicants.*



---



## JOB DETAILS FIELDS



| Field | Entry |

|---|---|

| **Job Type** | Full-time (or part-time 20 hrs/week to start, see notes) |

| **Salary** | AUD $1,200 to $1,500 per month, depending on portfolio and test task |

| **Hours** | Mon to Fri, overlapping 9am to 5pm AWST (Perth runs on the same clock as Manila) |

| **Category** | Advertising / Marketing / Creative |

| **Skills** |
 Ads, Meta Ads Manager, Copywriting, Direct Response, Funnels, Canva, Reels, Shorts, Video Editing, Creative Strategy, UGC, Market Research, AI Tools, ClickUp, Hubstaff |



---



## JOB DESCRIPTION (paste this section)



### About us



Genghis Digital is a digital marketing agency based in Perth, Western Australia. We run Meta and Google Ads, build websites and CRMs, and generate leads for clients across coaching, health, trades, construction, finance and hospitality.



We're a small remote team. You'd work directly with me (Marlon, the founder), alongside our media buyer, web builder and designer.



### What this role actually is



I'll be upfront, because it saves us both time.



At the moment I'm the one doing the research, working out the angle, writing the hook and d
 what we test. I hand that over, and what comes back matches the brief but has no idea behind it, with copy that reads like it came straight out of ChatGPT. That part of my week is what I want to hand off.



So the job is this. You get a client, an offer and an ad account, and you come back with ads you can defend. Angles you picked for a reason, written in words an actual buyer would use.



If you need a finished brief in front of you before you can start, this will frustrate both of us. Better you skip it.



### What you'd own



Research. Going through the client's offer, their competitors' ads, reviews, sales call notes, form responses,
 groups, anywhere the buyer's own words show up. You come back with the objections and the language.



Angles. Working out what belief needs shifting, and for who.



**Funnel stage creative.** This is the part that matters most. A top of funnel ad, a middle of funnel ad and a bottom of funnel ad are three different jobs. Cold traffic needs a problem named and something that stops the scroll. Middle of funnel needs the mechanism, the proof and the objections handled. Bottom of funnel needs the offer, a reason to move now and the risk taken off the table. If all three come back looking much the same, we've got a problem.



Copy. Hooks, primary text, headlines, calls to action, in plain language. Single most important skill in this role.



Statics, built in Canva. They don't need to win awards. They need to stop the scroll and be readable on a phone.



**Video, also built in Canva.** Scripted, cut and captioned by you. Vertical 9:16 for Reels and Shorts is our default format. Talking head, UGC style, screen recordings, slideshows, whatever suits the angle. Our team works in Canva so files stay shared and editable, which makes Canva video skills essential here. Other editors are a bonus, not a substitute.



Reading the numbers. Hook rate, hold rate, CTR, cost per lead. Telling me what's dying and what you want to try next, before I have to ask.



Turnaround. When I flag something, it gets sorted in your next work session rather than next week.



### What a normal week looks like



It varies. Some weeks are one client and a new offer to go deep on, others are a refresh across a few accounts. What stays consistent:



- New creative across all three funnel stages for the clients you're on

- A research or angle doc whenever a new client or a new offer lands

- A short note each week covering what's working, what's dead and what you want to test next



You d
 what gets made. I sign off on it, I don't spec it for you.



### What you need



- At least two years making Meta ads with real budget behind them. Not spec work, not organic social posts

- **A working understanding of funnels**, with examples of ads you've built for different stages

- Copywriting that sells. You know why "unlock your potential" does nothing

- **Strong Canva skills across both statics and video.** Not resizing templates, actually building

- Comfortable in Ads Manager reading results at creative level

- Written English good enough to write ads for an Australian audience. It doesn't need to be flawless, but it needs an ear for how people actually talk

- Sensible use of AI (more on that below)

- **A computer running at least two screens, ideally three.** I'm being direct about this because it isn't a preference. You'll be across Ads Manager, Canva, research tabs, transcripts and ClickUp at the same time, and doing that on one monitor slows the work to a crawl. If you don't have the setup now, tell me in your application and we'll sort it out before you start

- Reliable internet, and you're reachable during AWST business hours



### How we work



We run the team on ClickUp and Hubstaff, so you need to be comfortable with both.



ClickUp is where tasks, briefs and creative sit. Everything gets tracked there, so I can see what's in progress without having to chase people for updates.



Hubstaff tracks your hours and takes periodic screenshots while you're working. I'd rather say that plainly up front than surprise you with it. It isn't about looking over your shoulder, it's how contractors get paid accurately and how I know a job is properly resourced. If that's not something you're willing to work with, this isn't the right fit and no hard feelings.



### Helpful, not essential



- Lead gen for coaching and service businesses. Health, fitness, gyms and nutrition make up a big share of our book, so experience selling to that market is a real advantage

- Google Ads

- GoHighLevel

- Pulling buyer language out of call recordings and form responses



### On AI



I want you using it. Research, competitor angles, summarising reviews and call transcripts, throwing up variations for you to react to, sorting through data. If it halves the time it takes you to get to a good ad, use it.



What I won't accept is raw AI output going out as the finished product.



The value is in what you do afterwards. Stripping out the generic phrasing, putting the buyer's real words back in, breaking up the rhythm that gives it away, adding the specific detail that only someone who did the research would know to include. Anyone can prompt. What I'm paying for is the judgement to spot when something has come back flat, and the skill to fix it.



If it reads like ChatGPT by the time it hits my inbox, it went out too early.



Tools are on us. Canva Pro, AI subscriptions, research tools, whatever the job needs. You shouldn't be paying for software out of your own pocket.



### Don't apply if



- Your application is AI written. Not because AI is banned here, but I need to hear how you think before I can work out how you'd use it. Rough English with a sharp idea beats polished English with nothing behind it, every time

- Your portfolio is logos, brand kits and Instagram grids. I need to see paid ads

- You need a full brief before you can get started



### What you get



- Long term ongoing work. I'm looking for someone who stays

- Every tool you need, paid for

- Paid on time, every time, through Wise

- A direct line to me, with no account managers in between

- Real budgets, real accounts and real data to learn from

- Room to grow into a lead creative role as the agency grows



---



## HOW TO APPLY (paste this too, it's the filter)



Should take you ten minutes. Miss a step and I won't read it.



**1. Subject line, in this format:**

`CREATIVE STRATEGIST, [Your Name], [best ad you've ever seen that you didn't make]`



**2. Three Meta ads you've made.** A link or screenshot of each, plus one line on the angle and which funnel stage it was for. Add the numbers if you have them.



**3. Write me two hooks.** Same offer, same business: an Australian gym owner selling a $5,000 coaching program to other gym owners.

- One hook for cold traffic who've never heard of him

- One hook for someone who's already had a sales call and hasn't signed

- One line on why they're different



Just the hooks. No design, no script, no document.



**4. Quick answers:**

- How do you use AI in your work, and what do you always do to it afterwards?

- How many monitors are you running, and are you fine with ClickUp and Hubstaff?



Every application that follows the steps gets read. Anyone shortlisted gets a paid trial on a live client account before we talk about anything ongoing.



---

---



# NOTES FOR MARLON (do not paste)



## 1. Sort out Denus's lane before you post



If this hire lands, Denus becomes execution only, producing from the strategist's briefs. That can work fine and it's cheaper than replacing him, but he should be told that's the structure rather than work it out on his own. Same goes for the referral you were messaging about. If she's a real strategist, send her the two hooks task before you post publicly. Ten minutes of her time, ten seconds of yours, and it might save you the whole hiring round.



## 2. On the salary



AUD $1,200 to $1,500 is roughly USD $780 to $980 at current rates, so worth checking the rate on the day. Genuine creative strategists on OnlineJobs.ph, the ones who research an offer and build the angle without a brief, generally sit around USD $1,000 to $1,600. Your range lands just under that.



You can still hire well at this number, but two things help:



Post the $1,500, not the range. People read a range as the bottom figure, and $1,200 puts you in editor and designer territory, which is the exact profile you're trying to get away from.



If you can't stretch, buy fewer hours instead of paying less per hour. Twenty hours a week at $1,200 reads as a senior part-time role and pulls a different applicant than forty hours at the same money. On that platform the rate signals seniority far more than the hours do.



Also check the currency dropdown when you post. 
 usually only offers USD or PHP. If AUD isn't there, put the USD figure in the field and state the AUD amount in the body so nobody can argue about it later.



## 3. Expect volume



You'll get well over a hundred applications and most will be templated. Sort on the subject line first, which clears out everyone who skim read. Then read nothing but the two hooks. Ignore the portfolios on the first pass, they all look the same and half are borrowed. Twenty minutes and you'll have your shortlist.



## 4. What the two hooks tell you



The whole test is in the gap between them. Cold traffic and a warm lead who's already had a sales call need completely different messages, so anyone who thinks in funnels will produce two hooks that barely resemble each other. Anyone who doesn't will hand you the same hook twice with a word swapped. That's your answer, and it takes ten seconds to see.



Second thing to look at is the language itself. The scenario is a gym owner selling to gym owners, so the hook should sound like a bloke who runs gyms. If it comes back as "unlock the growth your gym deserves," they've either used AI or they write like AI on their own, and either way it's the problem you already have.



## 5. Always run a paid trial



One live client, a fixed fee, an agreed set of creatives. Pravar or Bowie would both work as a test. Nothing in an application tells you whether someone can research an offer without you holding their hand. Only a trial on your own accounts does that.



## 6. On AI in the application



There's no AI-proof test, and chasing one will cost you good applicants. The two-hook task is deliberately short, so someone can paste it into ChatGPT in seconds. That's fine. AI writes generic hooks, and generic is exactly what you're screening out, so it fails the test on its own merits rather than needing to be caught.



If you do want to check, put the task in a Google Doc, give edit access, and look at File then Version history. Typed writing appears as hundreds of small edits, pasted AI appears as one block landing in a second. Worth the effort at shortlist stage, not before.

We're hiring ONE full-time Inbound Appointment Setter to call warm leads from our
 and Instagram ad campaigns for a color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California.



This is NOT cold calling. Every lead you speak to has already raised their hand by submitting their info through one of our ads. Your job is to reach them fast, build trust quickly, understand what they actually want, and guide them into a booked appointment.



This role demands two things at once: sharp conversational judgment AND tight process discipline. The conversations are where you win or lose the booking. The process — cadences, call dispositions, CRM hygiene, follow-up tasks — is what makes the whole system work and what lets us measure anything. You need both. People who are great at one and sloppy at the other don't last here.



On the conversation side, what we're really hiring for is the ability to think on your feet. Someone replies three days later with just "sorry, been busy." Someone says they want highlights but describes something else entirely. Someone says "that's a bit far for me" but what they really mean is they don't see why it's worth the drive. If you can read what people actually mean and move the conversation forward without being told what to say next, you'll do well here.



If you need to be spoon-fed a script for every situation, this won't work.



IF YOUR BACKGROUND IS PRIMARILY CUSTOMER SERVICE OR VIRTUAL ASSISTANT AND NOT SALES, PLEASE DO NOT APPLY.



OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses).

13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top.



---



ABOUT THE COMPANY



You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years.



The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market.



You'll work directly under Ethan, the founder of Midnight Siren — no middle managers, no agency layers between you and the person making decisions. The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at salon handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked.



A note on team structure: you will be the only appointment setter on the team. Your day-to-day working relationship is directly with Ethan. There are no peer-level coworkers, no team chat with other appointment setters, no group energy to feed off. If you thrive with autonomy, clear systems, and a direct manager relationship, this works well. If you need a team environment or peer social dynamic to stay motivated, this will feel isolating over time.



We're in an active scaling phase. Core processes exist and are being refined. They don't change daily, but they evolve as we learn. If you like improving systems alongside a team, you'll fit. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't.



---



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING



This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support.



Daily:



- Call new
/Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day)

- Run our call script for the structured parts of the call, and use our frameworks + your own judgment for discovery and objection handling. The script covers the greeting, the offer, pricing, and the booking ask. Discovery can't be fully scripted — clients say what they say, and you'll need to adapt in real time.

- Respond to inbound SMS,
 
, and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them

- Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel

- Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar

- Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs

- Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM)

- Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers



Weekly:



- One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min)

- Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings

- Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them



During training (first 2–4 weeks):



We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence.



---



A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY)



We use a script. We also need you to think.



Where the script is fixed: the greeting, how we introduce the salon, how we present the offer, how we state pricing, the booking ask, and our core objection responses. These are tested and they work. You run them as written. Your tone, warmth, and pacing are what make them sound human — not changing the words.



Where the script can't help you: everything a real client throws at you. A vague text with no context. A client describing a service using the wrong name. Someone who's hesitant but won't say why. Someone who asks about price before you've figured out what they actually want. There is no script for these. There's a framework, and there's your judgment.



This is the part people underestimate. A big chunk of this job is not reciting — it's listening to what someone actually means and figuring out the next move in seconds, while they're on the phone with you.



Scripts do change here, but only based on data. If you bring an idea for a better line, we'll A/B test it. If it wins, it becomes the script. What we don't do is let setters freelance changes on the fly, because then we can't measure what works.



If you want to be told exactly what to say in every situation, this role will frustrate you. If you like having strong structure AND room to think, you'll do well.



---



SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES)



All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning.

- US workdays: Monday through Friday

- US days off: Saturday and Sunday

- Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call)

- Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST



Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March):



Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT

- A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time

- A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time

- Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night)



Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November):



- Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT

- Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH



This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit.

Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying.



---



COMPENSATION



Base pay:



$900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month.



13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000.



Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly):



- $3 per new client showed appointment

- $2 per existing client showed appointment

- $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon)



Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly):



- +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month

- +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month

- +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month



Worked examples:



Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950 (midpoint)

- Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90)

- Threshold bonus: $75

- Total: ~$1,250/month



Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950

- Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120)

- Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150)

- Total: ~$1,475/month



Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked):

- Base: $1,000

- Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking)

- Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350)

- Total: ~$2,025/month



This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role.



---



OTHER BENEFITS



1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year

2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can.

3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation.



To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form



---



TARGET KPIs



- Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+

- Show Rate: 90%+

- Bookings per day: 4–9

- Showed appointments per month: 100–160

- Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit.



---



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



Background:



- Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders.

- Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required.



Non-negotiable skills:



The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for:



- Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role.

- Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings.

- Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going.

- Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe.

- Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists.



Everything else:



- ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier.

- STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work.

- Typing speed: 50 wpm minimum (65+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application.

- Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind.

- Script discipline for the structured parts of the call.

- Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused.

- Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified.

- Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising.

- Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance.

- CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred.

- High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one.

- Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing.

- Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load.



Preferred:



- Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry

- Personal interest in beauty or self-care

- Experience working with older female clientele (35–65)

- Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster)



Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT):



We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean:



- Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout.

- Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words.

- Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat.

- Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down.

- Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses.

- KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them.



---



TECH REQUIREMENTS



Non-negotiable:



- Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire.

- Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application.

- Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop

- Mouse

- Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods.

- Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls.

- Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients.



Preferred:



- Second monitor

- You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster)



---



DO NOT APPLY IF:



- You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a 
nt to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait.

- You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it.

- You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next.

- You type slowly. Under 50 wp
ans you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking.

- Your background is primarily customer service, general VA work, or admin support with no direct sales or appointment setting experience. This role requires proven experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment. Customer service experience alone is not sufficient.

- Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker

- You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast.

- You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure

- You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating"

- You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it"

- You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term

- You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation



---



HIRING PROCESS



1. Application via Tally form (link below) — includes voice recording, Loom video, internet speed screenshot, backup plan description, and a few short written questions

2. 20-minute pre-screen call with our hiring partner

3. First-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — includes live roleplay

4. Second-round interview with Ethan (~45 min) — final fit + offer discussion

5. Offer — targeting hires between August 10 – August 20

6. Paid training begins immediately after offer acceptance



---



HOW TO APPLY



Submit your application through this Tally form: | 
 |



IMPORTANT: There is a confirmation requirement embedded in this post. Applications that miss it will be skipped regardless of experience.



The form will ask for:



- A screenshot of your typing test results (
)

- A screenshot of your internet speedtest (speedtest.net)

- A screenshot of your computer specs (RAM and processor)

- A description of your backup plan for power/internet outages

- A few short questions to gauge fit

- A short voice recording (Vocaroo or similar)

- A short Loom video introducing yourself



Applications submitted via direct messages on OnlineJobs.ph will NOT be reviewed. Use the Tally form.



---



Looking forward to meeting the right person.



Ethan

Founder, Midnight Siren



---



Full-Time | Long-Term | Remote | Pacific Time (Graveyard Shift in PH)

The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for:



- Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role.

- Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings.

- Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going.

- Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe.

- Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists.



Everything else:



- ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier.

- STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work.

- Typing speed: 50 wpm minimum (65+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application.

- Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind.

- Script discipline for the structured parts of the call.

- Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused.

- Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified.

- Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising.

- Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance.

- CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred.

- High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one.

- Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing.

- Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load.



Preferred:



- Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry

- Personal interest in beauty or self-care

- Experience working with older female clientele (35–65)

- Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster)



Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT):



We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean:



- Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout.

- Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words.

- Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat.

- Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down.

- Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses.

- KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them.



---



TECH REQUIREMENTS



Non-negotiable:



- Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire.

- Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application.

- Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop

- Mouse

- Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods.

- Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls.

- Quiet, dedicated workspace. No roosters, no karaoke neighbors, no babies crying, no traffic, no dogs barking during calls. We will hear it on the call, and so will our clients.



Preferred:



- Second monitor

- You already own a headset that meets the requirements above (we'll provide one if you don't, but having your own helps you start faster)



---



DO NOT APPLY IF:



- You struggle to think quickly and respond in real time. If you need a 
nt to figure out what to say, this role will be painful. Clients don't wait.

- You need the client to lead the conversation. If you're comfortable answering questions but not steering, this isn't it.

- You can't hold a conversation without a script telling you what to say next.

- You type slowly. Under 50 wp
ans you'll fall behind on notes and texts while you're talking.

- Your background is primarily customer service, general VA work, or admin support with no direct sales or appointment setting experience. This role requires proven experience persuading people, handling objections, and closing toward a booked appointment. Customer service experience alone is not sufficient.

- Your spoken English is hard to understand on the phone — this is a phone role first and the single biggest dealbreaker

- You're juggling multiple clients or planning to freelance on the side. THIS MUST BE YOUR ONLY JOB. We track performance closely and will discover this fast.

- You want a high guaranteed salary with low performance pressure

- You don't like high call volume or you find scripts "suffocating"

- You see remote work as "work whenever you feel like it"

- You can't sustain a graveyard shift long-term

- You're looking for a short-term gig — we expect a minimum 12-month commitment after probation



---



HIRING PROCESS

• Stable high-speed internet connection

• A reliable computer capable of handling large RAW files

• Backup internet or power arrangements are highly desirable



Experience with twilight conversions, virtual staging, floor plans or video editing would be valuable but is not essential.



HOURS AND COMPENSATION



• Full-time remote position

• Approximately 38 hours per week

• Working schedule to be agreed, with some overlap with Australian business hours

• Expected rate: A$4.50–A$10 per hour, depending on experience, speed and editing quality

• Initial four-week paid trial

LEAD THE CREATIVE OPERATION. THEN HELP BUILD WHAT COMES NEXT.

Creative Production is the center of this role at the start. You will manage the editors, own the production system, raise the quality of the work, and make sure strong creative moves from brief to final asset without senior leadership having to manage every detail.



This is not a coordinator role. It is not a virtual-assistant role. We need a Marketing Operations Manager who can operate the day-to-day work and improve the system at the same time.



A NOTE FROM OUR CMO

Before applying, watch this short video from our CMO about the role, its expectations, and what success looks like:


/share/9cd974e7c8a848de8b84a4a992df4e45



Once Creative Production is stable and you have demonstrated the judgment, leadership, and capacity required, the role will expand into Social Media Operations. That second phase will include the team, publishing, community, creator, affiliate, and channel systems around the content.



Phase 2 is planned to begin 60–90 days after your start date. The exact timing will depend on demonstrated readiness and business needs.



ABOUT VERITAS

Veritas builds complete Starlink Mini deployment setups—mounts, power, cables, cases, and accessories—for consumers, work teams, and government fleets.



We are a growing US company with a small, high-output marketing team in the Philippines. Several team members have grown with the company over the long term. We want the same for this role.



THE DETAILS

• Full-time independent contractor role with fixed monthly compensation of $2,000–$2,500 USD, based on experience, leadership depth, and overall fit—not an hourly position

• Approximately 45–50 hours per week, with the regular work schedule fully aligned with Pacific Time

• Philippine graveyard shift: roughly 11:00 PM–8:00 AM or 12:00 AM–9:00 AM, depending on U.S. daylight saving time

• Fully remote and long-term

• This must be your only job. No part-time employment, side hustles, ongoing freelance clients, or subcontracting

• Occasional weekend availability when production, launches, or publishing require management coverage

• Metro Manila, Rizal, Bulacan, Cavite, or Laguna required; no regular onsite office days, but occasional in-person meetings may be scheduled



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

At full production, the team aims to produce one long-form video and up to 14 supporting creative assets each week. These may include shorts/reels, static graphics, or carousels and are adapted for distribution across
, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X.



PHASE 1: LEAD CREATIVE PRODUCTION

• Manage a two-person video-editing team, including their priorities, workload, deadlines, coverage, development, and performance.

• Turn approved priorities into clear production plans, briefs, scripts, storytelling direction, B-roll needs, and deliverables.

• Own the production pipeline: capacity, assignments, dependencies, revisions, blockers, asset readiness, and delivery visibility.

• Review short-form, long-form, ads, thumbnails, static assets, carousels, platform versions, and other creative output.

• Evaluate the full story—not only whether one shot matches one line. Check hooks, pacing, B-roll, demonstrations, captions, CTAs, factual accuracy, brand alignment, and viewer flow.

• Give editors clear, prioritized, actionable feedback and verify that required revisions were completed correctly.

• Use performance findings to identify stronger hooks, packaging, formats, V2/V3 opportunities, and creative tests.

• Build and improve SOPs, review standards, production trackers, asset repositories, AI-assisted QA, and backup coverage.

• Coordinate minor corrections and urgent production support when needed, without turning the role into a primary editing position.



PHASE 2: ADD SOCIAL MEDIA OPERATIONS

Phase 2 is planned to begin 60–90 days after your start date, once Phase 1 is operating reliably and you have demonstrated readiness for the expanded scope. At that point, you will also:

• Manage the current Social Media Moderator and future social media team members.

• Own the publishing calendar, content inventory, platform schedules, launch pushes, and publishing verification across
, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X.

• Ensure each platform receives the correct version, copy, CTA, description, tags, products, related content, links, and native-platform setup.

• Oversee community, marketing inboxes, important comments and messages, channel presentation, and routine reputation handling.

• Manage routine creator-partnership and affiliate operations, including communication, records, deliverables, logistics, and escalation.

• Own routine UTM, Bitly, campaign-link, profile-link, and destination-verification workflows.

• Review social performance and turn findings into decisions, tests, and coordinated creative recommendations.

• Build and maintain the social department’s processes, AI workflows, reporting, and continuity systems.



HOW THE ROLE FITS

You will report to and work closely with senior marketing leadership. In Phase 1, the video editors report to you. In Phase 2, the Social Media Moderator also reports to you.



You will have authority over routine departmental planning, assignments, quality, coaching, corrections, and process improvements within approved standards. Cross-functional, sensitive, contractual, financial, policy, staffing, reputation, and other material decisions remain with senior leadership.



HOW WE USE AI

Our marketing operation uses AI for context, research, briefs, feedback, quality control, documentation, analysis, automation, and institutional memory.



We want someone who uses AI heavily to improve judgment and execution—not someone who accepts raw output. Sources must be checked. Brand and product accuracy must be protected. What the team learns should improve the next workflow.



YOU'RE A STRONG FIT IF YOU

• Have at least eight years of professional work experience.

• Have at least three years managing teams and direct reports.

• Have at least two years of experience inside a creative or marketing function.

• Have meaningful corporate, in-house, agency, or field-based operating experience—not only freelance, VA, or task-based remote experience.

• Have managed a creative-production pipeline and can explain the team size, volume, process, problems, decisions, and results.

• Are exceptionally strong at storytelling and can diagnose why an edit is technically correct but still wrong for the overall story.

• Hands-on video-editing experience is an advantage, but it is not required. You must be able to direct editors, evaluate their work, and clearly explain what needs to change and why.

• Can coach editors, address recurring mistakes, manage underperformance, and maintain accountability without becoming the bottleneck.

• Take action without waiting for step-by-step direction and consistently look for ways to improve quality, speed, visibility, and continuity.

• Use performance evidence to improve creative work—not only report numbers.

• Use AI daily with structured context, validation, human review, reusable systems, and feedback loops.

• Communicate clearly in conversational American English.

• Can sustain a Philippine graveyard schedule and occasional weekend coverage.

• Reside in Metro Manila, Rizal, Bulacan, Cavite, or Laguna and be willing to attend occasional in-person meetings.

• Have reliable primary internet, a backup connection, and backup power.

• Want one company to grow with for the long term.



THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR

• Someone who waits for detailed instructions before acting.

• Someone whose experience is limited to task-based VA work, short freelance engagements, or managing multiple clients.

• A strong individual contributor who does not want to manage, coach, and hold people accountable.

• Someone who reviews only technical editing details but cannot evaluate the complete story and business goal.

• Someone who creates more process without improving output, visibility, quality, or results.

• Someone planning to keep another job, freelance clients, or subcontract any part of the work.

• Someone testing a graveyard schedule for the first time without a credible plan to sustain it.



HOW WE WORK

Clear priorities. Direct feedback. Strong ownership. Problems are raised early. Decisions are documented. The goal is not to look busy. The goal is to build work that performs and an operation that improves.



Our brand voice follows the same standard: short words, short sentences, confident but never salesy. Like a friend who knows the gear.



HOW TO APPLY

Use this subject line and at least 20 AP:

[INSERT REQUIRED WORD] - [X] years of professional experience - [X] years managing teams



Include the following:

• Your resume with company names, employment dates, role titles, team sizes, and whether each role was corporate, in-house, agency, freelance, or VA work.

• Have you directly managed a creative-production or video-production team? Answer Yes or No. If yes, state the team size.

• Can you provide examples of videos, campaigns, or creative projects you directly led if you advance to the next stage? Answer Yes or No. Do not send links or detailed explanations at this stage.

• In one short logistics block, confirm that this would be your only job and that you would complete all work personally. Include your city or province, most recent U.S.-hours role and actual schedule, primary and backup internet, backup power, and occasional weekend availability.



Note: Applications missing any requirement will not be considered.

title: Full-Time YouTube Video Editor
description:
# Full-Time YouTube Video Editor



## Financial Education and Entrepreneurship Content



We are looking for a highly skilled, full-time video editor to join our team and work exclusively with our brands.



This is not a freelance project or agency position. We are looking for one dedicated editor who can work 30–40 hours per week and consistently produce high-quality long-form and short-form content for YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, and other social media platforms.



## What You’ll Be Editing



Our content focuses on:



* Business funding and credit

* Trading and investing

* Entrepreneurship

* Financial education

* Business growth

* Personal development and success stories

* Interviews, webinars, and educational presentations



Your primary responsibility will be editing long-form YouTube videos. You may also repurpose those videos into short-form content for YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, and TikTok.



## Responsibilities



* Edit engaging long-form YouTube videos

* Turn raw footage into clear, professional, high-retention content

* Repurpose long-form videos into short-form clips

* Remove pauses, mistakes, filler words, and unnecessary sections

* Add captions, graphics, screenshots, B-roll, sound effects, and music when appropriate

* Use punch-ins, pattern interruptions, and visual changes to maintain attention

* Create strong hooks during the opening seconds of each video

* Improve pacing without removing important context

* Clean up audio and maintain consistent sound levels

* Follow our brand guidelines and editing style

* Organize footage, project files, and completed videos

* Make revisions quickly based on feedback

* Meet daily and weekly production deadlines

* Communicate clearly with our content and marketing team



## Required Experience



You must:



* Speak and understand English fluently

* Have professional long-form YouTube editing experience

* Have edited financial, trading, credit, investing, business, or entrepreneurship content

* Understand how to make educational financial content interesting and easy to follow

* Understand YouTube retention, pacing, hooks, and storytelling

* Know how to edit both horizontal and vertical content

* Be experienced with Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut Pro, or comparable professional software

* Have a reliable computer and high-speed internet connection

* Be available to work 30–40 hours per week

* Be able to complete videos consistently without missing deadlines

* Be willing to work exclusively with our company



## Do Not Apply If



* You are an agency

* You plan to outsource the editing

* You are currently managing several clients

* You only have experience editing short-form content

* You have never edited financial or business-related videos

* You struggle to understand spoken English

* You require constant supervision to complete assignments

* You regularly miss deadlines or disappear during projects



## What We Are Looking For



The right person is:



* Creative but able to follow direction

* Fast without sacrificing quality

* Reliable and consistent

* Detail-oriented

* Comfortable receiving feedback

* Interested in financial education and entrepreneurship

* Able to identify strong moments without being told where every cut should go

* Interested in becoming a long-term member of our company



This is a long-term opportunity. We want someone who can learn our voice, understand our audience, and help us build one of the strongest financial education content brands online.



## How to Apply



Please submit:



1. Your name and location

2. Your weekly availability

3. The editing software you use

4. Your expected monthly compensation

5. Three examples of long-form YouTube videos you personally edited

6. Examples of financial, trading, business, credit, or investing content you edited

7. One example of short-form content you edited

8. A short explanation of how you improve viewer retention

9. Confirmation that you are not an agency and will personally complete the work

10. Confirmation that you can work exclusively with our company for 30–40 hours per week



Begin your application with the words **“FINANCIAL VIDEO EDITOR”** so we know you read the entire description.

description:
Senior Bookkeeper SME

Role Overview

We are seeking a highly experienced Senior Bookkeeper SME to provide technical expertise

across full-cycle bookkeeping and accounting operations for multiple offshore clients across

different industries. The role requires strong accounting fundamentals, advanced accounting-

system knowledge, analytical judgment, and the ability to independently manage complex

bookkeeping, reconciliation, closing, and process-related requirements.

reconciliations, and financial reporting support.

• Perform bank, credit card, AP, AR, and GL reconciliations, investigate discrepancies, and

resolve or properly document outstanding items.

• Support month-end and year-end closing, including accruals, prepaids, fixed assets,

depreciation, and adjusting entries.

• Review financial records, P&L, Balance Sheet, and General Ledger for accuracy,

completeness, and unusual or unsupported activity.

• Perform bookkeeping cleanup, catch-up, corrections, and reclassifications when

required.

• Work with accounting platforms such as QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, and other

ERP/accounting systems.

• Handle connected cloud platforms such as 
, Shopify, Amazon, ADP, online

banking, payment platforms, and similar applications.

• Maintain accurate master data, accounting records, and supporting documentation.

• Create and maintain SOPs, process documentation, workflows, and troubleshooting

guides.

• Identify process gaps and recommend improvements to increase accounting accuracy,

efficiency, and consistency.

• Serve as a technical SME and escalation point, providing guidance and quality review to

bookkeeping team members when needed.

• Manage multiple client accounts across different industries while maintaining deadlines,

accuracy, and client-specific requirements.

• Communicate effectively with clients and internal stakeholders regarding accounting

issues, requirements, discrepancies, and deliverables.



Core Competencies

• Full-cycle bookkeeping expertise

• Strong knowledge of Banking, AP, AR, GL, Fixed Assets, and master data maintenance

• Strong understanding of month-end and year-end closing

• Advanced proficiency in accounting software and cloud-based financial platforms

• Strong reconciliation, discrepancy investigation, and financial analysis skills

• Process documentation, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement

• Ability to manage multiple offshore clients across different industries

• Advanced Excel/Google Sheets skills

• Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills

• Strong written and verbal English communication

• High level of independence, ownership, and attention to detail



Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Accountancy, Accounting, Finance, or a related course.

• At least 5 years of relevant bookkeeping/accounting experience.

• Strong hands-on experience in full-cycle bookkeeping.

• Proven experience with accounting software, preferably QuickBooks Online.

• Strong understanding of reconciliations and core accounting functions.

• Experience supporting month-end closing.

• Ability to work independently in a remote/offshore, multi-client environment.

• Strong communication and documentation skills.



Preferred Qualifications

• Supervisory, team-lead, reviewer, or SME experience.

• Experience in an accounting firm, BPO/shared-services, CAS, or outsourced

bookkeeping environment.

• Experience handling multiple offshore clients across different industries.

• Certification or advanced proficiency in QBO, Xero, NetSuite, or similar platforms.

• Experience with 
, Shopify, Amazon, ADP, online banking, payment platforms,

and accounting integrations.

• Experience with multi-entity, multi-currency, inventory, payroll, fixed assets, or

intercompany accounting.

• Experience supporting CPA reviews, audits, financial reporting, or tax requirements.



Good-to-Have Skills

• QBO/Xero certification or advanced platform expertise.

• Exposure to US GAAP/IFRS.

• Experience in accounting-system implementation, migration, automation, and process

improvement.

• Advanced data analysis and familiarity with AI tools for accounting and productivity.

• Experience mentoring, reviewing, or providing technical guidance to bookkeeping

teams.



Success Profile

The successful Senior Bookkeeper SME should be able to independently manage full-cycle

bookkeeping, maintain accurate and reliable financial records, complete reconciliations and

closing activities, investigate and resolve discrepancies, navigate multiple accounting systems,

improve accounting processes, and provide technical guidance across multiple client accounts.

The ideal candidate does not simply process transactions—they understand the accounting

behind them, identify when something does not make sense, investigate why, and take

appropriate action.



For interested candidates, please send the following:

2. Introduction Video
